narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you drove this outcome most strongly. First, the size of the loan you requested had the strongest negative influence. At 10,961 DM and for a 48-month term, both the amount and the duration were far above the averages seen among approved applicants (roughly 3,000 DM and 19 months). The model viewed this large, long-term commitment as a substantial risk.

Second, your savings balance worked in your favor. Having more than 1,000 DM puts you in the top few percent of applicants and strongly pushed the prediction toward approval. Unfortunately, this positive factor was not enough to offset the concerns created by the loan size.

Third, your four-to-seven years of steady employment also helped your case, pulling the prediction toward good credit. While this is a solid employment record, it still could not overcome the dominant impact of the requested loan amount and length.

The bank therefore concluded the overall risk was too high. To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a substantially smaller loan with a shorter repayment period. This single change would remove the largest negative signal the model saw in your file.
